events.title: Opening of the Stockton and Darlington Railway
events.description: The Stockton and Darlington Railway in northeast England opened, with George Stephenson's locomotive Locomotion No. 1 hauling the first train. It was the first public railway to use steam locomotives to carry both goods and passengers.
events.significance: Marked the beginning of the modern railway age, transforming transportation, trade, and industrialization worldwide.

events.title: William the Conqueror Sets Sail for England
events.description: William, Duke of Normandy, set sail from Saint-Valery-sur-Somme with his invasion fleet after weather delays, landing at Pevensey on September 28.
events.significance: Led to the Norman Conquest and the Battle of Hastings, permanently reshaping English language, law, culture, and aristocracy.

events.title: Pope Paul III Recognizes the Society of Jesus
events.description: Pope Paul III issued the bull Regimini militantis Ecclesiae, formally approving the Jesuit order founded by Ignatius of Loyola and his companions.
events.significance: The Jesuits became a major force in education, missionary work, and the Counter-Reformation, with global influence in scholarship and science.

events.title: Google Founded
events.description: Google is commonly cited as having been founded on September 27, 1998 (though the company often celebrates other dates), when Larry Page and Sergey Brin, Stanford PhD students, began operating the search engine as a company.
events.significance: Google grew into one of the world's most influential companies, fundamentally changing how people access information and shaping the modern internet economy.

events.title: Constantine I of Greece Abdicates
events.description: King Constantine I of Greece abdicated the throne following the Greek defeat in the Greco-Turkish War and a military coup, and was succeeded by his son George II.
events.significance: Reflected the national crisis after the Asia Minor Catastrophe and contributed to political instability that led to the abolition of the Greek monarchy in 1924.
